assumptions.rule: An exact normalized company-name match to one SEC issuer may supply an estimated historical identity. A ticker alone is insufficient.
assumptions.consequence: These links remain assumptions; recycled symbols and unrecognized name changes remain unresolved.

assumptions.rule: Recover dated primary schedules from cached filings. Only a separately labeled sensitivity assumes a structured action was observable by its effective-day close.
assumptions.consequence: An effective-day proxy cannot support an announcement-entry claim. Its first simulated entry is the following session.

assumptions.rule: Missing signal values use the median of earlier observed other issuers, one latest observation per issuer, or neutral 50/100 before peers exist. No balance-sheet amount is filled with zero.
assumptions.consequence: Estimated ratings are separate from reported financial scores. Missing evidence reduces conviction and widens the net-edge uncertainty allowance.

assumptions.rule: When the issuer's last as-filed period is 201–550 days old, reuse its historical signals as estimates before using other issuers. Assume the last annual operating burn persists and subtract elapsed burn from last cash, floored at zero, before computing runway.
assumptions.consequence: Unreported financing or improving operations could invalidate this cash-depletion estimate. Old reported amounts and projected cash are separate; none are promoted to a fresh reported score.

assumptions.rule: Assess all 27 routes. Quantitative evidence can support six deterioration mechanisms; filing passages remain context leads. Unresolved mechanisms contribute no extra positive edge.
assumptions.consequence: Provisional conviction is rating × (0.35 + 0.65 × observed numerical fraction) × 0.75, with a further 0.8 identity-assumption multiplier. The 0.75 discount reserves for unresolved valuation/catalyst underwriting. It is not a probability. Fraud and bad-actor conclusions are never inferred.

assumptions.rule: A reverse split changes units and creates zero economic dilution by itself. Model possible new issuance at 0%, 15% or 30% discounts, including the cash raised in per-share value.
assumptions.consequence: Financing scenarios guide comparable matching and risk disclosure; their effect is not added a second time to historical short returns.

assumptions.rule: Fill gaps only with real free daily charts. Undo later split adjustments and check overlapping nominal observations. Existing provenance-bound nominal prices take priority.
assumptions.consequence: No synthetic entry, exit, delisting return or fill. Unresolved admitted paths invalidate performance. Public reconstructed prices are not official auction evidence.

assumptions.rule: Before the entry exists, use the last known closing price projected into the share units of the already-announced split, assuming no economic price move.
assumptions.consequence: The plan is an estimate. Actual opening price and portfolio capacity are assessed separately at entry; future price data never enters the announcement plan.

assumptions.rule: Compare 0.1% and 1% of prior average share volume, plus a $25 versus $100 minimum. Retain whole shares, fees, margin and the 2% aggregate +200% squeeze-loss budget.
assumptions.consequence: Validated public daily volume can replace explicitly partial three-venue counts, with historical nominal volume units assumed. Larger participation adds a square-root impact allowance. These are capacity sensitivities, not evidence of available borrow or fills.

assumptions.rule: Use earlier other-issuer measured depth where available. Otherwise use a spread floor of max(0.5%, one cent / price), plus 2 × prior daily volatility × sqrt(order / prior daily dollar volume).
assumptions.consequence: The fallback is an explicit cost assumption with an extra uncertainty reserve; twice-slippage cases are also replayed.

assumptions.rule: Use a prior public daily borrow proxy within 24 hours when present, with an assumed historical symbol link. Otherwise use 50% annualized. Double and sixfold fee scenarios scale both proxies and the fallback. Fees apply to rounded collateral across forecast settlement-to-return calendar days, including weekends.
assumptions.consequence: If no fresh entry proxy exists, a stale announcement rate cannot reduce the fallback: use the greater of that last indication and the fallback, scaled in stress cases. Rates are not charges or approvals. The strict case admits nothing without an actual entry locate and execution evidence.

assumptions.rule: Show a further 2% of starting capital squeeze-loss deduction and 50% borrower-access thinning using an identity-seeded ex-ante selection, without optimizing the seed.
assumptions.consequence: A stop is not a guaranteed loss limit; no hypothetical tail event is described as an observed historical event.

assumptions.rule: Import public dividend events as modeled payment-in-lieu costs when held across the ex-date. Unknown corporate cash adjustments remain uncovered.
assumptions.consequence: Fractional split settlements and complete dividend coverage still require actual records.

baseline_comparison.limits: Recovered daily opens are price observations, not fills or independent new trades. The repaired study deduplicates source records and applies separate cost and conviction assumptions; its P&L is not a data-only comparison with RSI-3.

plan.selection: Coverage/cost comparisons declared before new results; prior exits remain explored.

strict_case.reason: Historical locate approval, fills and full underwriting cannot be assumed into observed evidence.

remaining: Incomplete event universe and ambiguous historical security identities.
Historical borrowed inventory, actual rates/charges, recalls and account approvals.
Historical NBBO, auction fills, halts and SSR-compliant order execution.
Fully reconciled warrants, convertibles, ATM issuance, valuation and catalysts.
Missing delisted prices, unobserved dividends and fractional corporate-action settlements.
